Missing-data handling: deterministic regression (conditional-mean OLS) imputation of the 4 missing predictor cells (grass 1, canopy 1, distance 2), with each imputation model fitted on originally observed rows (predictors + Season) and applied to originally missing cells; no rows excluded, n = 351 of 351. Native scale: log rate ratio per one percentage point of total grass cover. Estimate = -0.01016 (rate ratio 0.9899 per pp), SE = 0.01250, test statistic z = -0.81, p ~ 0.42, inferential df = 17 (property clusters - 1). Observation unit: one quadrat visit; design: quadrats nested within 18 properties, crossed with 3 survey rounds (properties recur, physical quadrats do not). Conclusion: weak, statistically non-significant negative association between grass cover and seedling recruitment. Caveat: outcome is highly overdispersed (mean 6.7, variance ~434) relative to the Poisson variance, but the GEE sandwich SEs remain valid for the population-averaged coefficient. Sensitivity checks (complete-case and global-median imputation) gave near-identical focal estimates (-0.0084 to -0.0102).
rows.predictor: Total grass cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover (percent cover of quadrat, raw percentage points); effect reported as log rate ratio of total eucalypt seedling count per one percentage point increase

rows.note: Negative binomial GLM (log link, alpha fixed at 1) of total Eucalyptus seedling count per quadrat visit on exotic grass cover. Outcome: euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (verified to match precomputed euc_sdlgs_all). rows.note: Logistic GLM of Eucalyptus seedling occurrence (binary: any seedling across the three height classes 0-50cm, 50cm-2m, >2m present in a quadrat) on z-standardized total grass cover. Grass cover = sum of ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover, standardized (mean 30.61 pp, SD 23.54 pp) within the analysis sample. Adjusted for eucalypt canopy cover (%), distance to nearest eucalypt canopy (m), and survey season (fixed effects, drop-first). rows.predictor: z-standardized total grass cover (sum of exotic annual, exotic perennial, and native perennial grass percent cover, standardized to mean 0, SD 1); estimate is log-odds change in seedling occurrence per 1 SD increase

Focal predictor: NativePerennialGrass_cover, native perennial grass percent cover in raw percentage points (as_declared: larger = more grass). Adjustment set: property fixed effects (18 dummies, absorbing site-level climate/soil/management), plus eucalypt overhead canopy cover (Euc_canopy_cover) and distance to nearest eucalypt canopy (Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m)) as seed-source proxies. Missing data: median imputation of the 4 missing covariate values (1 native grass, 1 canopy, 2 distance); no rows dropped, n=351 quadrat visits. Inference: cluster-robust standard errors clustered on Property (18 clusters). Focal result: estimate -0.02597 log-rate-ratio per percentage point of native perennial grass cover, SE 0.02834, z = -0.916, p = 0.36, df_resid = 330. No evidence that native perennial grass cover influences recent seedling recruitment (CI spans both directions). Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat visited in one of three survey rounds; quadrats do not recur across rounds. Fitted in statsmodels GLM IRLS with cov_type='cluster'.
rows.predictor: NativePerennialGrass_cover (native perennial grass percent cover of the quadrat, raw percentage points)

rows.note: Negative binomial GEE (log link, alpha=1, exchangeable working correlation, robust sandwich SEs clustered on Property) of total eucalypt seedling count per 15x15 m quadrat visit. Outcome: euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (verified equal to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all). Focal predictor: exotic grass cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover, in raw percentage points. Covariate adjustment: litter cover, bare-ground cover, and survey season (microsite/contextual adjustment set); seed-source/canopy covariates deliberately not included per frame constraint. Missing data: listwise deletion of rows missing any model variable (1 of 351 rows excluded; n=350, 18 property clusters). Estimate on native log-rate-ratio scale: -0.006642 per percentage point of exotic grass cover (SE 0.013332, robust z = -0.498, p = 0.618, df_resid = 344). Interpretation: about 0.7% lower expected seedling count per additional percentage point of exotic grass cover, but the CI includes zero; no detectable effect. Observation unit: quadrat-visit. rows.predictor: Exotic grass cover: ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover, in percentage points of quadrat area (effect on log expected seedling count per 1 percentage point)

Adjusted for Euc_canopy_cover, Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m), and Season (survey round). Exclusions: listwise deletion of rows missing any model variable (3 of 351 rows excluded; n=348 used; observation unit = one quadrat visit; properties recur across rounds but quadrats do not). Result: estimate -0.007718, robust SE 0.008077, z = -0.956, p = 0.339, 95% CI [-0.024, 0.008] — a non-significant negative association; roughly 0.8% lower expected seedling count per additional percentage point of exotic grass cover. Conclusions consistent across earlier robustness fits (negative binomial GLM: -0.0125, SE 0.0103; Poisson GLM cluster-robust: -0.0137, SE 0.0099). df_resid = 342; statistic kind: z (Wald).
rows.predictor: Exotic grass cover, defined as the sum of ExoticAnnualGrass_cover and ExoticPerennialGrass_cover, expressed in percentage points of quadrat ground cover; coefficient is the log-rate-ratio of total eucalypt seedling count per +1 percentage point of exotic grass cover

Observation unit: one quadrat-visit. Focal effect (native log-count scale): log-rate ratio = -0.006329 (SE 0.012000, z = -0.527, p = 0.598; exp(beta) = 0.9937, i.e., ~0.6% fewer seedlings per additional percentage point of grass cover), 95% CI approx [-0.030, 0.017]. Overdispersion confirmed (outcome mean 1.86, variance 38.5; NB2 alpha = 5.23), justifying negative binomial over Poisson. Result: little evidence that grass cover influences Eucalyptus seedling recruitment in this sample; the point estimate is negative (more grass, fewer seedlings) but statistically indistinguishable from zero. df_resid = 326; test statistic is a cluster-robust z.
rows.predictor: Total grass cover in percent of quadrat area = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover; coefficient is the log-rate ratio of eucalypt seedling count per +1 percentage point of grass cover

Response: total Eucalyptus seedling count per quadrat = euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m. Focal predictor: NativePerennialGrass_cover in raw percentage points; focal estimate is the log rate ratio of expected seedling count per +1 percentage point of native perennial grass cover (native model scale, log). exp(estimate)=0.9886. Test statistic: z = -0.456, p ~ 0.648; inferential df = 17 (clusters - 1); n = 348; observation unit = one physical 15x15 m quadrat visited in one survey round (quadrat-visit). Caveats: strong Poisson overdispersion (mean 6.7, var ~434), but robust GEE sandwich SEs are valid for the population-averaged coefficient. rows.predictor: NativePerennialGrass_cover (raw percent of quadrat): log-rate-ratio of total Eucalyptus seedling count per +1 percentage point of native perennial grass cover

EXPOSURE: ExoticAnnualGrass_cover alone (percent of quadrat), single untransformed class, chosen after both the all-grass sum and the exotic-grass sum were excluded; annual exotic grasses are the dominant grass layer in these grazed remnant woodlands and the growth form most implicated in competitive suppression of seedling establishment; good contrast (mean 12.4%, range 0-76, 46 zero quadrats). MODEL: GLM y ~ ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + Euc_canopy_cover + Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m) + C(Season), family=Binomial(logit), property-cluster-robust SEs (18 clusters). FOCAL ESTIMATE (native log-odds scale): -0.00725 per +1 percentage point of exotic annual grass cover, SE 0.01110; t = -0.653 with small-sample df = 17 (clusters-1), p = 0.52; OR = 0.993, 95% CI (0.970, 1.016). EXCLUSIONS: 3 rows dropped listwise for missing cover/canopy/distance values; n = 348 of 351; no missing seedling counts. INFERENCE: No statistically detectable effect; point estimate slightly negative (more grass, weakly less recruitment). Estimate sign consistent across all four specifications run in this trajectory (all-grass on 0-50cm count: -0.01234 SE 0.01031; exotic sum on count: -0.00617 SE 0.01923; exotic sum on presence: -0.01435 SE 0.00977; exotic annual on presence: -0.00725 SE 0.01110), none significant; the combined exotic-grass presence specification carried the strongest signal, suggesting the perennial exotic component drives most of the weak association. Per-property spatial covariates (climate/soil/radiation) intentionally omitted as collinear with the property cluster absorbed by cluster-robust SEs. Script: scripts/annualgrass_logit.py.
rows.predictor: ExoticAnnualGrass_cover (percent of quadrat covered by exotic annual grass, single class, no transformation); effect reported per +1 percentage point on the log-odds of seedling presence

rows.note: Poisson GEE (population-averaged) with exchangeable working correlation and robust sandwich covariance, clustered on Property (18 clusters). Missing data: 350 of 351 rows used; the 1 row missing the focal grass predictor was excluded (not imputable without biasing the estimand); rows missing adjustment covariates (2 missing distance-to-canopy) were retained via property-median imputation. Test statistic: z = -0.43, p = 0.67; inferential df = 17 (clusters - 1); n = 350; observation unit = one quadrat visit in one survey round; design = rounds x fresh random quadrats nested within 18 properties. Native scale: log rate-ratio per one percentage point of exotic annual grass cover (rate ratio per pp = 0.996). Estimate is essentially null with slight negative sign: grass cover shows no detectable effect on seedling recruitment. Caveat: outcome strongly overdispersed relative to Poisson variance, but GEE sandwich SEs remain valid for the population-averaged coefficient under variance misspecification.
rows.predictor: ExoticAnnualGrass_cover (percent ground cover of exotic annual grasses in the quadrat, raw single-column measure, untransformed; coefficient is log rate-ratio in expected Eucalyptus seedling count per one percentage point increase)

rows.note: Outcome: total Eucalyptus seedling count per 15x15 m quadrat visit, summed across all three height classes (euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m). Model: negative binomial (NB2) GLM with log link, fitted by maximum likelihood with the dispersion parameter alpha estimated jointly (alpha = 187.7, reflecting extreme overdispersion; three properties had zero seedlings, giving separated fixed effects that carry no recruitment information). Within-property dependence handled by property fixed effects (17 dummies for 18 properties); standard errors are model-based (not cluster-robust). Adjustments: Euc_canopy_cover, Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m), Season (survey round). Listwise deletion of 3 rows with missing model variables: n = 348 quadrat visits across 18 properties (Winter 2006, Spring 2006, Autumn 2007; physical quadrats differ each round). Native scale: log rate ratio per one percentage point of total grass cover; focal estimate = -0.00310 (95% CI -0.0213 to +0.0151), z = -0.333, p = 0.74, residual df = 325. Conclusion: no detectable effect of grass cover on Eucalyptus seedling recruitment; each additional percentage point of grass cover multiplies expected total seedling count by exp(-0.00310) = 0.997. Result stable across BFGS and Newton optimizers. Caution: alpha is large and the count distribution is zero-inflated, so power is limited. Observation unit: one quadrat in one survey round. Design: nested field survey, properties as spatial clusters, repeated rounds with non-overlapping quadrats.
rows.predictor: Total grass cover, in percentage points of the 15x15 m quadrat, computed as ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover; the focal estimate is the log rate ratio of total eucalypt seedling count per one percentage point increase in this sum.

Focal estimate: log-rate change per one percentage point of exotic grass cover = -0.02003 (rate ratio 0.9802 per pp), SE = 0.01394, z = -1.436, p = 0.151, df: asymptotic (z), inferential clusters = 18. Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat visit; design: 351 quadrat visits (non-persistent quadrats) nested in 18 properties across three survey rounds (Winter 2006, Spring 2006, Autumn 2007); properties recur across rounds, physical quadrats do not. Conclusion: exotic grass cover shows a negative but statistically null association with established Eucalyptus seedling recruitment at conventional levels. Sensitivity note: alternative constructions (any-occurrence logit; size-weighted index; total grass cover across all three grass classes) all yielded small negative, null estimates, so the direction is robust across specifications.
rows.predictor: Exotic grass cover, percentage points of quadrat ground area (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover); effect is per one percentage point, log-rate scale

Response = sum of the three seedling height classes (euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m). Adjustment set: Euc_canopy_cover (percent), Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m), and Season (survey round, factor). Exclusions: listwise deletion of rows missing any model variable (3 of 351 rows dropped; n = 348 quadrat-visits). Focal estimate is native log-link scale: log-rate-ratio per one-unit increase in ln(1 + exotic annual grass cover percent) = +0.00145 (SE 0.13494, z = 0.011, p = 0.99, df = 17 = 18 clusters - 1); i.e., essentially null. Caveat: outcome strongly overdispersed (mean 6.7, variance ~434) relative to the Poisson variance, but the GEE robust sandwich SE remains valid under variance misspecification. Consistent with the earlier raw-scale fit (coef -0.004/pp, SE 0.009, also null). Observation unit: one quadrat visit; design: quadrats nested within properties, properties recurring across three survey rounds, quadrats not resampled.
rows.predictor: log(1 + ExoticAnnualGrass_cover): natural log-plus-one of exotic annual grass percent cover (raw percent of quadrat ground area)

Outcome: total eucalyptus seedlings per quadrat visit = euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (verified equal to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all). Focal predictor: exotic grass cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover, in percentage points, unsigned as constructed; larger values = more grass = as_declared orientation. Adjusted for Euc_canopy_cover, Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m) (renamed dist_euc for formula parsing), and Season (3 rounds). Property entered as fixed effects (17 dummies), absorbing all property-attached covariates (climate, soil, management) and between-property dependence; HC1 SEs address overdispersion/heteroskedasticity. Exclusions: listwise deletion of missing model variables removed 3 of 351 rows (n=348); 3 all-zero-recruitment properties (Olive, Rokahr, Taylor) contribute nothing to the within-property likelihood under the log link, so the fitted n is 298 quadrat visits across 15 properties, df_resid=278. Focal estimate: +0.004041 per percentage point of exotic grass cover on the log-rate-ratio scale (z=0.446, p=0.66), i.e., a null within-property grass-cover effect; the coefficient is identified purely from within-property variation in grass cover. Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat sampled in one survey round (fresh random quadrats each round; quadrat labels not persistent). Result robust in direction to marginal alternatives (cluster-robust NB and Poisson, and exchangeable-correlation GEE) gave small negative marginal estimates, indicating earlier associations were driven by between-property contrasts; the within-property estimate reported here is the most conservative and least confounded quantity.
rows.predictor: Exotic grass cover, percent points: ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover

rows.note: Negative binomial GLM (log link, alpha fixed at 1.0), statsmodels IRLS, on 348 of 351 rows (3 excluded listwise for missing values). Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat visit; design: quadrats nested in 18 properties across three survey rounds (Season fixed effects). Outcome: total Eucalyptus seedlings per quadrat = euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m (verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all for all rows). Native scale: log rate-ratio per one percentage point of exotic annual grass cover. Estimate = -0.007642, SE = 0.012639, z = -0.605, p = 0.545, residual df = 342, n = 348. Conclusion: no detectable effect; point estimate slightly negative. Caveat: NB dispersion fixed at alpha=1 rather than profile-estimated; property-clustered SEs were used, so spatially-derived covariates (climate/soil/radiation) were not separately included to avoid collinearity with the cluster structure.
rows.predictor: ExoticAnnualGrass_cover (percent ground cover of exotic annual grass, one percentage point; log rate-ratio on total eucalypt seedling count per quadrat)

Outcome construction: euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m. Focal estimate is on the model's native log(count+1) scale: +0.000912 per percentage point of native perennial grass cover (SE 0.003152, t = 0.289, residual df ~ 342, p ~ 0.77; exp(coef) = 1.00091) — an essentially null, slightly positive association. Property random-intercept variance 0.146 vs residual 0.599 confirms real between-property clustering. Robustness: alternative operationalizations of grass cover (all-grass sum and exotic-grass sum) under Poisson GEE fits with property-clustered robust SEs gave small non-significant negative coefficients (e.g. -0.0084, SE 0.0116); the log-linear mixed model gives a small non-significant positive coefficient — all support a null effect of grass cover on Eucalyptus seedling recruitment in these data.

Response: total Eucalyptus seedlings per 15x15 m quadrat-visit (sum of euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m; verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all). Nuisance structure: property fixed effects (18 dummies, absorbing all property-level confounding: soil, climate, seed-source context, management) + Season (survey round) factor. Missing data: the single row with missing grass-cover components (1 missing per grass column, same row) was handled by within-property median imputation rather than deletion; outcome counts and Season/Property were complete, so n = 351 of 351 rows. Estimate = -0.009110 (SE 0.011662, z = -0.781, p = 0.435; exp(beta) = 0.9909), i.e. about a 1% lower expected seedling count per extra percentage point of grass cover, not statistically distinguishable from zero. Overdispersion confirmed (seedling mean 1.85, variance 38.4; NB2 alpha = 5.55), justifying NB over Poisson. Caveat: three properties (Olive, Rokahr, Taylor) recorded essentially zero seedlings everywhere, so their fixed effects tend to -infinity (incidental zeros) and they contribute no within-property information to the grass coefficient; identification comes from within-property covariation. Observation unit: one quadrat sampled in one round; quadrats do not persist across rounds and quadrat labels are not persistent IDs. Design: nested survey, 18 properties (spatial clusters, used for FE and clustered SEs) x 3 rounds (Winter 2006, Spring 2006, Autumn 2007), ~351 quadrat-visits total. Test statistic: z (large-sample Wald, cluster-robust); inferential reference: standard normal (df = 18 clusters inform the cluster-robust variance but the Wald test is asymptotic). An alternative defensible specification (adjusting for eucalypt canopy cover and season with listwise deletion instead of property FE) gave a nearly identical result (-0.0113, SE 0.0098), indicating the null-ish negative association is robust to confounding/missing-data handling.

Outcome: count of established Eucalyptus recruits taller than 50 cm per quadrat (euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m; mean 1.2, max 21, 80/351 quadrats nonzero). Poisson dispersion was 4.27, so negative binomial was used (moment-based alpha, floored at 0.01). Focal predictor: NativePerennialGrass_cover, raw percent cover of the quadrat (one percentage point = 1% of 15x15 m quadrat area). Adjusted for Euc_canopy_cover, Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m), and Season (survey round, dummy-coded, drop-first). Standard errors: cluster-robust by Property (18 clusters). Exclusions: listwise deletion, 348 of 351 rows used. Focal result: log-rate change per percentage point of native perennial grass cover = +0.01346 (SE 0.01105, Wald z = 1.218, p = 0.223; rate ratio 1.0136 per pp). Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat visit (quadrats not revisited across rounds). Design: cross-sectional nested survey — quadrats clustered within 18 properties, 3 survey rounds (Winter 2006, Spring 2006, Autumn 2007); inference carried by property-clustered SEs. Estimate is on the native log-rate scale; larger values of the predictor mean more grass cover, so orientation is as_declared. Across alternative specifications (total grass cover, exotic grass cover, occurrence, size-weighted index) estimates ranged from -0.020 to +0.013 per pp, all statistically null at conventional thresholds.
rows.predictor: NativePerennialGrass_cover — percent ground cover of native perennial grass in the 15x15 m quadrat (raw percentage points); effect expressed as log-rate change in established (>50 cm) Eucalyptus recruit counts per one percentage point increase

rows.note: Model: logistic binomial GEE (population-averaged) with exchangeable within-property working correlation and robust (sandwich) covariance, clustered on Property (18 clusters). Outcome: binary occurrence of recruitment — presence of ≥1 Eucalyptus seedling in the 0–50 cm height class per 15×15 m quadrat visit (prevalence 11.7%). Focal predictor: total grass cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover (percentage points of quadrat ground cover); larger values = more grass, as_declared. Adjustment set: Euc_canopy_cover (%), Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m), and Season (survey round, categorical). Missing data: property-median imputation for the few missing covariate values (1 grass/canopy cover value, 2 distances; outcome fully observed), so all 351 quadrat visits retained — no listwise deletion. Result: log-odds ratio per percentage point of grass cover = 0.00173 (SE 0.01103; z = 0.157, p ≈ 0.88; 95% CI −0.020 to +0.023; odds ratio per pp = 1.0017). Test statistic: Wald z = 0.157. Inferential df: 17 (clusters − 1). Fitted n = 351; observation unit = one 15×15 m quadrat in one survey round; design = nested cross-sectional survey, quadrats clustered within 18 properties, three seasonal rounds (Winter 2006, Spring 2006, Autumn 2007), physical quadrats not resampled across rounds. Conclusion: no detectable grass-cover effect on seedling-recruitment occurrence in the native log-odds scale; the interval excludes neither moderate negative nor moderate positive effects. Sensitivity: an earlier Poisson GEE on total seedling counts (before the outcome change) gave a similarly null, slightly negative estimate (−0.0084 log rate ratio per pp), and the listwise-deleted version of this logistic model was essentially identical (0.00162, SE 0.01108), so the result is stable across outcome construction and missing-data handling.
rows.predictor: Total grass cover (percent of quadrat ground), constructed as ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover
